info.name: Oura (aifitnessapi.com)
info.description: Oura: OAuth 2.0 and Webhook samples requests built from the vendor documentation aifitnessapi.com quotes. Generated by scripts/build-collections.mjs; no secrets included. https://aifitnessapi.com/collections

item.name: OAuth 2.0
item.description:
Oura's authorization-code flow as its documentation describes it, read 2026-11-05. Fill client_id, redirect_uri and scope in an environment of your own and keep client_secret there, never in a shared collection.

The same facts, with each source sentence, at https://aifitnessapi.com/integrate/oura-api and https://aifitnessapi.com/tools/oauth-playground.

request.description:
https://cloud.ouraring.com/oauth/authorize. Authorization URL. Open this URL in a browser (in Postman: copy it from the request bar); the user signs in and Oura redirects to {{redirect_uri}} with ?code=… Put that value in the auth_code variable.

Source: Oura API documentation, “Authentication”, https://cloud.ouraring.com/docs/authentication

Scope: Space-separated. Left blank, the app requests every scope; the user can switch scopes off at consent. Source: Oura API documentation, “Authentication”, https://cloud.ouraring.com/docs/authentication

Documented scopes (joined with spaces):
- email: Email address of the user
- personal: Personal information (gender, age, height, weight)
- daily: Daily summaries of sleep, activity and readiness
- heartrate: Time series heart rate for Gen 3 users
- workout: Summaries for auto-detected and user entered workouts
- tag: User entered tags
- session: Guided and unguided sessions in the Oura app
- spo2: Daily SpO2 Average recorded during sleep
- heart_health: Heart health data (listed in the OpenAPI document, not on the Authentication page)

PKCE: Recommended. code_challenge_method must be S256; the verifier is 43 to 128 characters, hashed with SHA-256 and base64url-encoded without padding. Generate a verifier and challenge in your browser at https://aifitnessapi.com/tools/oauth-playground and put them in code_verifier and code_challenge. Source: Oura API documentation, “Authentication”, https://cloud.ouraring.com/docs/authentication

Also documented: https://developer.ouraring.com/authorize. Universal-link authorization URL for new OAuth clients; on a phone with the Oura app it can open the consent page in the app. Source: Oura API documentation, “Authentication”, https://cloud.ouraring.com/docs/authentication

https://api.ouraring.com/oauth/token. Token URL.

Source: Oura API documentation, “Authentication”, https://cloud.ouraring.com/docs/authentication

Client credentials go in the form body here; the vendor also accepts HTTP Basic.

Token lifetime: Returned in expires_in. The page states no fixed number for the server-side flow; the client-side flow's token is currently 30 days and has no refresh token. Source: Oura API documentation, “Authentication”, https://cloud.ouraring.com/docs/authentication

Note: Client credentials go in the form body or as HTTP Basic (client_id as user name, client_secret as password). Source: Oura API documentation, “Authentication”, https://cloud.ouraring.com/docs/authentication

Note: Every request to the Oura API needs a non-empty User-Agent header, so the commands below send one. Source: Oura API documentation, “Authentication”, https://cloud.ouraring.com/docs/authentication

Note: Revoke a token with GET https://api.ouraring.com/oauth/revoke?access_token=…. Source: Oura API documentation, “Authentication”, https://cloud.ouraring.com/docs/authentication

urlencoded.description: Enable when the authorization request carried a code_challenge.

request.description:
Refresh: grant_type=refresh_token at the token URL returns a new access token and a new refresh token; each refresh token works once.

Source: Oura API documentation, “Authentication”, https://cloud.ouraring.com/docs/authentication

item.name: Webhook samples
item.description:
Oura's documented example notifications, sent to {{local_url}} (your local handler) unchanged. Signature: HMAC-SHA256 keyed by your client secret over the x-oura-timestamp value followed by JSON.stringify(body), hex, upper-case, in x-oura-signature. Source: Oura API v2 OpenAPI document (1.43), “Webhooks for Real-Time Data Updates”, https://cloud.ouraring.com/v2/static/json/openapi-1.43.json

Headers that carry a signature hold the placeholder Oura prints, so a handler that verifies signatures will reject these: to send correctly signed requests, use https://aifitnessapi.com/webhooks/send-sample.mjs. Respond: Respond with a 2xx in under 10 seconds and process the event asynchronously. Before events flow, Oura verifies the callback with a GET carrying verification_token and challenge; echo the challenge as JSON.

Payload library with JSON Schemas: https://aifitnessapi.com/webhooks#oura.

request.description:
Oura sends a POST to your callback URL when subscribed data changes (the example: a user syncs new sleep data).

Oura's example event is a POST with x-oura-signature and x-oura-timestamp headers. Source: Oura API v2 OpenAPI document (1.43), “Webhooks for Real-Time Data Updates”, https://cloud.ouraring.com/v2/static/json/openapi-1.43.json

variable.description: Your app's client ID, from the vendor's developer console.
Keep it in a Postman or Bruno environment marked secret. This collection ships it empty.
The redirect URI registered with the vendor.
Scopes to request, joined as the vendor documents (see the authorization request).
A random value you check on the redirect.
The refresh_token from the token response.
